transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Wu (CTO - Cedarbridge), Maria Alvarez (Head of Security), Tom Reed (Platform Eng)

Summary: short sync to align on SOC 2 / ISO27001 evidence pathways — deep dive on encryption/KMS, how Redwood surfaces audit logs (lineage, export), and RBAC/SSO integration patterns. Collect immediate asks for pilot.

[00:00] Alex Moore: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this should be about 45 to 60 minutes, um quick intros then we can jump into the KMS and log question, um Priya is our solutions engineer who's gonna cover the technical flow.
[00:18] Daniel Wu: thanks Alex, yeah Daniel here, CTO. We're trying to lock down evidence collection for our SOC 2 readiness and want to make sure the redwood setup won't be a blocker for ISO.
[00:30] Maria Alvarez: hi all, Maria, head of security. My main concerns are key custody, audit log lineage, and proving chain-of-custody for tokens and user actions.
[00:45] Priya Singh: great, hey Maria — we can go through how Redwood's private deployment and dedicated options map to those controls. Quick note: some transcribed names might be off, like our internal product names sometimes show as Red wood or red wood runtime in the export, you'll see that.
[01:05] Tom Reed: hi Tom here. I'm the one who'll probably provision the VPC / network bits. I want to understand egress and where the logs live.

Topics / context gathering:
[01:20] Alex Moore: quick qualification — are you planning hosted API, dedicated reserved, or Private/VPC on-prem?
[01:28] Daniel Wu: leaning private in our cloud — we want data to stay in our VPC and keys in our KMS. We may evaluate Dedicated if we need RD throughput, but first priority is data residency and KMS control.
[01:40] Maria Alvarez: and we need to produce evidence for SOC 2 Type II next quarter; ISO 27001 is parallel planning for later in the year.

KMS / Encryption discussion:
[02:00] Priya Singh: ok cool. On Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS via an envelope key flow — Redwood supports AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, and can integrate with HSM via standard PKCS11 or an HSM-backed gateway. Practically you can keep the root keys in your KMS/HSM; Redwood will hold only ephemeral wrapping keys in memory for inference.
[02:25] Maria Alvarez: can you show me the diagram? The auditors will want key custody proof and rotation logs.
[02:33] Priya Singh: yes, I'll send a clear diagram. Quick caveat, the transcript may say KV cache instead of K V cache sometimes — that's a transcription quirk.
[02:40] Alex Moore: we have a KMS integration diagram in the trust center -- link: https://app.redwood.ai/trust-center/cedarbridge (note: demo link, permissions required). Priya will attach a static PNG and an HSM notes doc.
[02:55] Daniel Wu: good. Also, what's the rotation cadence and can we force rotate for audit?
[03:05] Priya Singh: rotation is driven by your KMS policy. For envelope keys we recommend a wrap-key rota of 90 days; root keys follow your org policy. We emit explicit key-use events to the audit log with key-id and operation.

Audit logs & log lineage:
[03:20] Alex Moore: next, logs. How does Redwood surface audit events?
[03:24] Priya Singh: we have a structured audit stream: request-level metadata, model selection, token counts, redwood user ids (service principals), and KMS ops. For Private we can push logs to your cloud logging endpoint (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Azure Monitor) or deliver TLS-syslog, plus a downloadable time-bound bulk export for auditors.
[03:45] Maria Alvarez: what about chain-of-custody? We need to show that logs weren't tampered with between service and storage.
[03:52] Priya Singh: we sign log bundles with a service certificate and provide checksums. For Private deployments you can route logs directly to your logging infra so custody stays in your environment. For hosted customers we keep signed bundles and a hydration proof. There's also an option for cross-checking hashes in the trust center.
[04:12] Tom Reed: also interested in lineage: if a user submits a prompt and then we later pull a transcript for the audit, is there a way to correlate model invocation -> underlying container -> GPU node ID?
[04:24] Priya Singh: yes — we include request_id, route_id, model_variant, node_id (anonymized in hosted), and process-id in the private deployment. For hosted, node_id might be obfuscated but you still get a stable invocation id and timeline. For private, you can map to container and instance id.

On RBAC / SSO:
[04:45] Alex Moore: let's touch SSO and RBAC quickly — what do you use today?
[04:50] Maria Alvarez: we use Okta for SSO and Azure AD for some internal services. We'd like SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[04:58] Priya Singh: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We also support IdP-initiated SSO and can map Okta groups to Red wood roles. For Private deployments we can optionally integrate with your AD via LDAP. Our role model separates platform admin, model-deploy, and billing roles — all mappable to SCIM groups.
[05:20] Daniel Wu: auditors will ask for RBAC matrix; can you export role assignments and SCIM change logs?
[05:27] Priya Singh: yep, you can export role assignment history and SCIM provisioning events. Those events are part of the audit log stream I mentioned.

Data residency / network controls:
[05:40] Tom Reed: question on VPC endpoints and egress — do we need NAT for Redwood to reach updates or is there a private peering option?
[05:48] Priya Singh: Private supports VPC peering and private link options; you can avoid public egress. For model updates we can push via your private endpoint. Some small host metadata calls may be required; we'll create a minimal allowlist. We'll share the allowlist as part of the network workbook.
[06:05] Alex Moore: note: we'll share the network workbook (spreadsheet) — current draft link: https://redwood.ai/network-workbooks/cedarbridge (permissions required).

Evidence collection and auditor workflows:
[06:20] Maria Alvarez: practical ask – for SOC 2 Type II we need sample evidence for the last 6 months: key rotation records, access change logs, and a snapshot of the RBAC matrix. Can Redwood provide time-series exports?
[06:34] Priya Singh: yes, we can produce time-bounded exports; for Private deployments exports come from your collector; for Dedicated/Hosted we provide signed bundles. We can also provide a guide (pilot runbook) which describes evidence snapshot steps for auditors.
[06:52] Daniel Wu: will you let our auditor read-only access to the trust center or to the log bundle?
[06:58] Alex Moore: we typically grant read-only trust center access to customer security leads. For auditor access we can either share signed bundles or issue a temporary reader account scoped to specific resources. We'll need a signed access request form.
[07:15] Maria Alvarez: OK, good. We'll need to get that form.

Transcription artifact notes / mis-terms:
[07:25] Priya Singh: FYI the transcript export may conflate KMS and KV cache in places; when we share the artifacts you'll see the corrected labels.

Detailed Q&A and clarifications (short snippets):
[07:40] Tom Reed: about retention — our policy is 7 years for audit logs for certain regulated lines; is that supported?
[07:46] Priya Singh: yes, we can configure long-term retention to your archive (S3 Glacier / Azure Archive). For long retention we suggest signed hash snapshots so you can prove immutability at any point.
[08:02] Maria Alvarez: will Redwood store PII in logs? We need to ensure minimal PII retention and redaction options.
[08:09] Priya Singh: by default we redacted user-submitted prompts in hosted but for private deployments you control whether prompt text is persisted. We also offer automated PII redaction in the export pipeline if you want us to redact sensitive fields before writing to your storage.
[08:30] Daniel Wu: what about encryption in transit between our VPC and Redwood endpoints?
[08:34] Priya Singh: TLS1.2+ and mutual TLS for private links. For hosted we use standard HTTPS; we can enable mTLS in dedicated/private for stronger guarantees.

Objections / tradeoffs:
[08:50] Maria Alvarez: I'm cautious about any hosted component touching unwrapped data — even ephemeral memory residency could be a concern for our audit panel.
[08:58] Alex Moore: totally — that's why Private with KMS-in-customer-control is the recommended path. We can also run a small on-prem package if that's necessary.
[09:08] Daniel Wu: cost vs control is the decision — we'll size the pilot accordingly.

Recap and explicit asks:
[09:20] Alex Moore: to recap — key deliverables from Redwood: 1) KMS/HSM diagram + key rotation note (Priya) 2) Trust Center Read access + sample SOC2/ISO export (Alex) 3) Network workbook and allowlist (Alex) 4) Pilot runbook for evidence collection (Priya). From Cedarbridge: prov VPC test endpoint, list of auditors, and internal SRE contact.
[09:44] Maria Alvarez: correct. Also need the access request form for temporary auditor accounts.
[09:50] Priya Singh: noted — I'll include the access request template in the packet.

Closing small talk / schedule:
[10:00] Alex Moore: we'll shoot the packet today and set up the pilot kickoff for week of 9/28. Any blockers?
[10:06] Tom Reed: none now, just need IP ranges.
[10:10] Daniel Wu: we'll get you the auditor list and internal contact by end of week.
[10:15] Maria Alvarez: thanks, talk soon.

References shared during call:
- KMS/HSM notes: will be attached to the follow-up email
- Trust Center link (provision after access): https://app.redwood.ai/trust-center/cedarbridge
- Network workbook (draft): https://redwood.ai/network-workbooks/cedarbridge
- Pilot runbook template: https://redwood.ai/pilots/evidence-runbook-template

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., 'KV cache' vs 'KMS'), speaker overlaps occasionally labeled awkwardly.

- Alex to share Trust Center read-only invite and a sample SOC2 export (due 2026-09-16).
